rationale: Every outstanding receipt is already interpreted, so the next judgment-changing action is to check whether the delivered finding is a RawNode-only curiosity: applications deliver peer messages through the public Node interface, whose Step is a different wrapper around the same filter. I register that as a child question and request one new fixed experiment (fifth test function) that drives a real Node started with RestartNode - goroutine, channels and Ready/Advance loop included - through the documented sequence: a real leader's real heartbeat, a local-type control from a peer, the peer-form MsgForgetLeader, and finally the intended local operation Node.ForgetLeader on the same node. The harness synchronizes on the node's own reported status rather than wall time and runs natively with the predicted observations; the formal reading waits for the receipt.

investigations.question: Does the same inbound gap exist through the public Node interface used by applications (Node.Step for messages received from peers), so that a peer-form MsgForgetLeader clears the leader context of a real Node, while Node.ForgetLeader remains the intended local producer of that same state change?
investigations.hypothesis: node.Step applies the same IsLocalMsg predicate as RawNode.Step, so a type missing from isLocalMsg passes into the receive channel and reaches the state machine, clearing the reported leader of a real Node; the difference from RawNode.Step is only that local types are ignored silently instead of returning ErrStepLocalMsg.
investigations.discriminator: Drive one real Node (RestartNode) with a real leader's real heartbeat, then compare three deliveries through the same public Step: a local type from a peer (leader must stay), the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (leader must not change if the filter covered the type), and the local API Node.ForgetLeader (which is allowed to change it).

scope.description: Fifth test function in the same harness file: a real leader is elected between two RawNodes (node 1 needs only its own vote plus node 3's), and the node under test is a real raft.Node with id 2 started by RestartNode from the same storage snapshot, with a goroutine consuming Ready/Advance. Observations are taken from Node.Status after the node's own run loop has processed each delivery.
assumptions: Applications deliver peer messages through Node.Step, which is the documented inbound path for messages received from other nodes.
A peer may construct a protobuf message of any type, including one that only the local API produces, with no term field.
Node.Status is a synchronized snapshot of the run loop's state, so polling it until the expected value appears measures the node's view rather than wall-clock timing; the poll count is reported.
All nodes share the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}).
excluded: Wall-clock latency: the harness polls up to a bounded number of milliseconds and reports the poll count.
Any multi-host transport behaviour; delivery is in-process through Node.Step.

experiment.prefix: Elect node 1 for real against node 3, deliver its real heartbeat to the real Node with id 2 through Node.Step and wait until the node reports lead=1; then deliver a local-type message (MsgCheckQuorum) from peer 3 and record the node's reported lead; then deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term) and wait until the reported lead changes; finally let the node hear the leader again, call Node.ForgetLeader and record the before/after lead. Every value comes from Node.Status (or the error returned by Node.Step/ForgetLeader), not from unexported state.
experiment.responsibility: The raft module owns which message types Node.Step accepts from the network and owns the meaning of the local ForgetLeader operation.

comparisons.description: Control: a genuinely local type delivered through Node.Step from a peer leaves the node's reported leader unchanged.
Defect predicate: a peer-form message type that the module itself only produces locally must not change the node's reported leader; a witness with lead_after=0 is the violated case.
Independent control: Node.ForgetLeader on the same node does change the reported leader (1 -> 0), which is why the network path must not reach that state change.
